dublinCore.title: Convolution
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Mathematics
Convolution
Overlap integral
dublinCore.description: Interactive introduction to convolution as a measure of overlap. A blue square slides across a stationary red triangle and the height of a purple gauge shows the area of overlap, the value of the convolution at the current position.

learningObjectives: Explain convolution as a measure of how much a sliding function overlaps a stationary one
Predict the slider positions at which the overlap begins, reaches its maximum and ends
Interpret the height of the purple gauge as the area of overlap, not the height of overlap
Calculate the overlap area at a given position from the geometry of the square and the triangle
Connect the sliding-and-overlapping picture to the convolution integral
prerequisites: Area under a curve as an integral

misconceptions.misconception: The gauge shows how high the two shapes overlap
misconceptions.correction: The gauge height is the area of overlap, not the height of the overlapping region
misconceptions.evidence: At slider 170 the overlap already reaches the triangle's full height, but the gauge is at half its maximum (area 0.25 of 0.50)

misconceptions.misconception: The purple triangle is the output signal
misconceptions.correction: The purple triangle is a gauge whose height is one value of the output at the current x; the output is the smooth bump traced by the gauge height as x changes
misconceptions.evidence: Plot the read-out against x for slider 140 to 260: the points form a rounded bump with a maximum of 0.50

misconceptions.misconception: Convolution multiplies the two functions at a single point
misconceptions.correction: At each x the product is a whole function of tau, and the output is the integral of that product over all overlapping points
misconceptions.evidence: Move the slider and watch the shared region change shape while only its area is reported

accessibility.screenReaderScript: A blue square slides across a red triangle. One slider sets the horizontal position of the square. The height of a purple triangle shows the area where the square and the triangle overlap, which is the convolution at that position, and the area is also printed as a number.

controls.label: x position of f(x)
controls.description: Slides the blue square from left to right across the red triangle; 60 slider units move it by its own width

visualElements.description: Blue square f(x) that slides and red triangle g(x) that stays fixed
Purple gauge triangle whose height is the area of overlap, with a dashed outline at the maximum
Read-outs of the overlap area, the maximum area and the offset x in square widths

model.description: Overlap area of a unit square and a unit triangle as the square is shifted; the area is summed over 200 thin slices of the square
equations: (f * g)(x) = integral f(tau) g(x - tau) d tau
area(x) = integral g(tau) f(x - tau) d tau

instructionalStrategies: Plot the read-out against x to reveal the output curve
extensions: Use the Convolution Visualizer to see the flip step and other signal pairs
